pick.headline: Deng Xiaoping begins US visit
pick.summary: On January 29, 1979, Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping began an official visit to Washington, the first by a PRC leader.
pick.significance: Deng's visit followed normalization and preceded China's attack on Vietnam by weeks. Moscow watched for an anti-Soviet alignment.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of January 29, 1979, listed "Press Comments on Deng Xiaoping's U.S. Visit" under Hungary and "Deng Xiaoping's Arrival in United States Reported" under Romania.

alternates.headline: Iraqi forces attack Khafji
alternates.summary: On the night of January 29, 1991, Iraqi forces crossed into Saudi Arabia and occupied the town of Khafji; Saudi, Qatari and US forces retook it by February 1.
alternates.significance: It was the only major Iraqi ground offensive of the Gulf War.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union contents for February 1991 listed, among Moscow comment on the Gulf war, KRASNAYA ZVEZDA's view that "Iraq's Attack on Khafji Has Psychological Aims", with items calling the U.S. "bogged down" and the hostilities protracted.

alternates.headline: France announces end of nuclear testing
alternates.summary: On January 29, 1996, President Jacques Chirac announced that France had permanently ended nuclear testing after a final series in the South Pacific.
alternates.significance: The resumed tests of 1995 had provoked worldwide protest. France then backed the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty signed later in 1996.
alternates.fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of January 31, 1996, carried Moscow ITAR-TASS: Foreign Ministry spokesman Karasin said Russia was "very much satisfied" with Chirac's decision to stop nuclear tests for good, calling it a major contribution to ending all testing.
